title: Wire failover orchestrator + region-signal-aggregator values, secrets, and rollout hooks
author: Benji Okafor
release_notes: Adds Helm chart wiring for failover-orchestrator and region-signal-aggregator, including required secrets, config schema, and staged rollout notes for monitor-only -> canary -> progressive failover.
body:
Summary: This PR adds Helm values/config wiring for the new failover automation components: (1) failover-orchestrator (state machine + audit events + override endpoints) and (2) region-signal-aggregator (ingests synthetic probes + metrics, normalizes into the region health contract). It also documents the required secrets, RBAC expectations, and a staged rollout sequence that matches Release Eng gating.

Context / why: The routing/control-plane work for automated regional failover is landing behind feature flags, but we were missing a coherent Helm integration for deployment across staging/prod clusters. In prior game day rehearsals we ended up doing manual patching of env vars and ad hoc secrets. This PR standardizes values, schema, and deployment defaults so we can run controlled failovers with repeatable configuration and auditability.

What’s included: - New chart: charts/failover-orchestrator/ - New chart: charts/region-signal-aggregator/ - Shared values conventions: global.region, global.environment, global.clusterName, global.audit (enabled/sink), global.telemetry (otlp endpoint), global.imagePullSecrets - ServiceAccount + RBAC templates for orchestrator (read routing policy store, write failover state transitions, post audit events) - Kubernetes Secret references (no secret material committed): * failover-orchestrator-secrets: ROUTING_POLICY_STORE_TOKEN, DNS_EDGE_API_TOKEN (staging/prod), AUDIT_SIGNING_KEY * region-signal-aggregator-secrets: METRICS_READ_TOKEN, SYNTHETIC_PROBES_API_KEY - ConfigMap wiring for signal contract and trigger parameters (monitor-only default): * health signal windows (default 1m/5m) * hysteresis + hold-down timers (defaults per Discovery) * safe-to-failover gating toggles (capacity + dependency health) - Optional ingress for orchestrator override endpoints (disabled by default; requires internal mesh policy) - PodDisruptionBudgets, resource requests/limits baseline, and topology spread constraints for both services - Rollout hooks: supports a “monitorOnly” mode for orchestrator; also supports enabling progressive failover only when the routing stack supports percentage-based routing.

Rollout plan (documented in chart README): 1) Staging: deploy both services with failover-orchestrator.monitorOnly=true; validate metrics + audit events + incident-bot linkage. 2) Prod (dark): same as staging, monitor-only, scoped to low-risk route/model via config (no traffic changes). 3) Prod canary: enable trigger evaluation + orchestrator transitions, but limit action to 1% canary failover for tier=dev/test customers (requires manual approval). 4) Progressive: expand by tier/route/model; require capacity headroom checks to pass.

Notes on secrets: This PR intentionally only references secret names/keys. Creating/updating the secrets is owned by Infra/SRE via terraform/secret manager; the chart README includes a checklist and a mapping table to the corresponding secret manager entries (names only).

Operational considerations: - Orchestrator override endpoints are disabled by default and require explicit enable + allowlist; they should be used only by on-call with the documented runbook. - The default values are conservative to avoid flappy failovers: hysteresis is enabled, hold-down timers default to 20m, and we require two independent “bad” signals before moving from DEGRADED->FAILOVER_CANDIDATE.

Testing: - chart lint (helm lint) - template rendering for staging/prod values (CI) - basic kubeconform schema validation for rendered manifests

Follow-ups (not in this PR): - Wire PodMonitor/ServiceMonitor objects once we finalize Prometheus operator adoption in all prod clusters (tracked in ENG-2847). - Add NetworkPolicy defaults for Private clusters (requires alignment with Private installer PR).

Screenshots/log excerpts: (1) Rendered manifest diff verified for staging; (2) Example values snippet in README showing monitor-only -> canary flip.

Links: - Linear: ENG-2843 / ENG-2844 / ENG-2847 - Related PRs: redwood#98248 (orchestrator state machine + audit logging), redwood#98412 (signal ingestion wiring)

Checklist: - [x] Helm lint passes - [x] Values schema documented - [x] Secrets required listed (names/keys only) - [x] Default is safe (monitor-only, no ingress) - [x] Reviewed by Release Eng for gating compatibility
commit_summaries: charts: add failover-orchestrator chart with configmap + secretRefs + rbac
charts: add region-signal-aggregator chart and values contract
docs: add rollout + secrets checklist to chart READMEs
ci: add kubeconform validation for rendered templates (staging/prod)
conversation:
Connor O'Brien (Release Eng): Can we make monitor-only the default everywhere and require an explicit enable for any action-taking behavior? Also, please document the exact flag flip sequence we expect during the prod controlled test window.

Benji Okafor (author): Yep. Updated defaults so failover-orchestrator.monitorOnly=true unless explicitly set false. Added a “Rollout sequence” section with the three values flips we expect (monitorOnly, allowAction, progressiveFailover.enabled) and where they’re permitted (staging -> prod-dark -> prod-canary).

Irene Choi (Infra Eng): Secret names look good, but please avoid implying the chart creates them. Can you add a warning banner in both READMEs and link to the internal secret provisioning runbook name (no URL needed)?

Benji Okafor (author): Added a WARNING at the top of both READMEs: chart expects secrets to exist; provisioning handled by Infra/SRE. Added reference to “Runbook: Secret provisioning for failover services (SRE)”.

Ethan Park (Control Plane): The orchestrator needs a stable identifier for audit trails (cluster + region + env). Can we ensure those fields are required and show up in labels/annotations too?

Benji Okafor (author): Added required global.clusterName + global.region + global.environment in values schema; plumbed into pod labels and audit event env vars (AUDIT_SOURCE_CLUSTER/AUDIT_SOURCE_REGION/AUDIT_SOURCE_ENV).

Miles Thornton (SRE/Architect): For safe-to-failover checks, we should default dependency gating on, capacity gating on, and keep thresholds conservative. Can you set those defaults and call out where they get overridden for game days?

Benji Okafor (author): Done. Defaults: safeToFailover.capacity.enabled=true, safeToFailover.dependencies.enabled=true. README includes a section “Game day overrides (temporary)” explicitly showing which keys may be adjusted with IC approval.

Tomáš Novák (SRE): Small nit: ingress should be off by default and annotated as internal-only when enabled. Also, can you add a note that override endpoints are audited and require on-call group membership?

Benji Okafor (author): Updated: ingress.enabled=false by default; when enabled, it uses internal ingress class + sets auth annotations placeholders. Added README note: override endpoints require RBAC group and all calls are logged to audit sink.

Sergio Costa (Observability) (drive-by): Any reason we don’t emit service labels consistently for dashboards (service=failover-orchestrator)?

Benji Okafor (author): Good call. Added app.kubernetes.io/name and app.kubernetes.io/component labels consistently.

Approvals: Connor O'Brien: Approved. Ethan Park: Approved. Irene Choi: Approved. Miles Thornton: Approved with comment addressed. Tomáš Novák: Approved.
